site.name: EcoScienceHub
site.tagline: Peer-informed writing on ecology, biology, and applied physics
site.description: Independent, scientifically literate writing on ecology, biology, and applied physics. Built to be read slowly and cited carefully.

ecology.label: Ecology
ecology.description: Long-form, peer-informed writing on the systems that sustain life — ecosystems and their services, the climate that shapes them, and the biodiversity that gives them resilience.

biology.label: Biology
biology.description: Cellular, molecular, evolutionary, and developmental biology — the mechanisms that connect a single sequence of bases to the diversity of living form.

physics.label: Applied Physics
physics.description: Applied physics for the climate transition and beyond — energy systems, thermodynamic limits, and the quantum foundations that increasingly matter outside the lab.

ecosystems.label: Ecosystems
ecosystems.description: Forests, wetlands, oceans, soils — how energy and matter move through living systems and what disturbance reveals about them.

climate-change.label: Climate Change
climate-change.description: Drivers, feedbacks, attribution, and the policy-relevant uncertainties at the frontier of climate science.

biodiversity.label: Biodiversity
biodiversity.description: Why species count is the wrong metric, what genetic and functional diversity actually do, and where conservation efforts are working.

earth-systems.label: Earth System Science
earth-systems.description: The planet as one coupled system — how the atmosphere, ocean, ice, land, and life exchange energy and matter, and what that coupling explains that no single component can.

earth-observation.label: Earth Observation
earth-observation.description: How satellites and sensors observe the planet — the methods, data products, and uncertainties behind measuring environmental change from space.

cells.label: Cell Biology
cells.description: The cell as the fundamental unit of life — its architecture, energetics, signaling, and the methods used to study it.

genetics.label: Genetics
genetics.description: Molecular genetics, genomics, and the evolution of genetic systems — what sequencing has revealed, what it cannot resolve.

evolution.label: Evolution
evolution.description: Selection, drift, development, and the modern synthesis — including the parts of it that are quietly being revised.

energy.label: Energy
energy.description: Generation, storage, transmission, and the materials and architectures that determine which technologies actually scale.

thermodynamics.label: Thermodynamics
thermodynamics.description: The laws that bound every physical system — and the surprisingly modern questions still open at their frontier.

quantum-basics.label: Quantum Basics
quantum-basics.description: Quantum mechanics for the practitioner — the parts that matter for sensors, materials, and computing, without the philosophy.

conservation.label: Conservation Science
conservation.description: Protected areas, species recovery, restoration, and invasive-species management — what conservation interventions achieve, and how that is measured.

oceans.label: Oceans & Marine Science
oceans.description: Ocean circulation, chemistry, productivity, and marine ecosystems — how the ocean works as a habitat and as a component of the climate system.

freshwater.label: Freshwater & Wetlands
freshwater.description: Rivers, lakes, groundwater, and wetlands — the smallest reservoirs in the water cycle and the most heavily used, and what determines their condition.

forests.label: Forests & Land Cover
forests.description: Forest structure, disturbance, carbon, and land-cover change — what forests do biologically and what they are counted as doing in carbon accounting.

soils.label: Soils & the Land Surface
soils.description: Soil formation, soil carbon, soil biology, and land degradation — the thin, slow-forming layer that most terrestrial life depends on.

pollution.label: Pollution & Environmental Quality
pollution.description: Air, water, and chemical pollution — sources, exposure pathways, measurement, and the evidence linking contaminants to ecological and human harm.

microbiology.label: Microbiology
microbiology.description: Bacteria, archaea, fungi, viruses, and the microbial communities that run most of the planet's biogeochemistry.

physiology.label: Physiology & Organismal Biology
physiology.description: How bodies work — respiration, circulation, thermoregulation, immunity, nervous systems, and development, in humans and other organisms.

taxonomy.label: Taxonomy & the Tree of Life
taxonomy.description: Naming, classifying, and reconstructing relationships among organisms — and the surprisingly unsettled question of how many species there are.

biotechnology.label: Biotechnology & Bioinformatics
biotechnology.description: Sequencing, genome editing, synthetic biology, and the computational methods that turn biological data into inference.

climate-physics.label: Atmospheric & Climate Physics
climate-physics.description: Radiation, atmospheric structure, convection, and the physics that determines how energy moves through the atmosphere and ocean.

mechanics-waves.label: Mechanics, Waves & Fluids
mechanics-waves.description: Motion, forces, energy, oscillation, sound, light, and the behaviour of fluids — the classical physics that underlies most measurement.

matter-radiation.label: Matter, Materials & Radiation
matter-radiation.description: Atomic and nuclear structure, radioactivity, particles, and the materials science behind detectors, reactors, and energy technologies.

home.meta_title: Peer-informed writing on ecology, biology, and applied physics
home.hero_title: Slow, careful writing about the systems that sustain us.
home.hero_lede: EcoScienceHub is a platform for ecology, biology, and applied physics — written by working scientists, edited for clarity, and cited where it matters. Built to be read slowly.
home.mission_title: Science is a slow conversation. We give it the room it needs.
home.mission_p1: Most of what passes for science writing today is optimized for the attention economy. Headlines outrun evidence; nuance is the first thing cut. We started EcoScienceHub because the alternative — careful, cited, accountable writing — is harder to find than it should be.
home.mission_p2: Every article on this platform is organized into a topic hierarchy (Topic → Subtopic → Article), written by a working scientist or experienced science journalist, and kept current with explicit revision dates. When we update something, we say so.
home.topics_title: Three lenses on the natural world

insights.title: Arguments worth defending
insights.description: Insights are short, structured essays. Each one stakes a single, falsifiable claim and defends it. They are written to be argued with — clearly, cited, and dated.

discussions.title: Curated scientific questions
discussions.description: Not a forum. Each entry is a question where the science is genuinely unsettled, framed by an editorial desk with the evidence on each side set out. There is no open commenting.
discussions.about_body: Each question is opened and framed by an EcoScienceHub editorial desk. The notes below the framing are editorial, written by the desk — they are not contributions from named researchers, and no comment on this site is from a member of the public. If verified external contributors take part in future, their entries will be marked and attributed to them by name.
discussions.closed_notice: EcoScienceHub does not accept public submissions on these questions. The notes above are editorial. If you work in one of these fields and want to contribute, write to info@helperg.com — a named contributor would be published under their own name and identified as such.

footer.footer_note: Editorially independent. Citations welcome — please link to the canonical URL.

newsletter.title: One careful piece a week.
newsletter.description: Subscribe to receive new long-form articles and insights, plus occasional notes from the editorial team. No clickbait, no list-buying, no tracking pixels.
